[0] everyday_reading (E): An everyday filter (a coffee filter) removes things. In the UNIX sense a filter is any program that reads standard input and writes standard output, even one that removes nothing.
[1] misconception (M) -> RedirectionIsArgument: wrong rule: The file a filter processes shows up in args[]. Right rule: A filter reads only standard input. The file or upstream program is attached by < or |, and args[] carries only parameters such as lo and hi.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> RedirectionIsArgument: Points to LT (read one value, test it, maybe print it, repeat). An uneven trace prints out-of-range values on some passes, or holds all the output until the end. (here mixing in: "a redirected file shows up in args[]")

[0] names_the_element (N): A filter is a program that converts a standard input stream into a standard output stream.
[1] states_the_rule (S): A filter reads from standard input and writes to standard output, classically writing a subsequence of its input (e.g. RangeFilter keeps the values between lo and hi).

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Each pass of while (!StdIn.isEmpty()) reads one value t, tests lo <= t <= hi, and prints t right away if the test passes. Output is produced while input is still being read.
[1] output_prediction (OP): `java RangeFilter 100 400` with input 358 1330 55 165 689 1014 3066 387 575 843 203 48 292 877 65 998 prints 358 165 387 203 292: the in-range values, in their original order.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One pass reads one value and appends it to the output only if it passes the test. lo and hi do not change.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Piping connects filters: the output of one becomes the input of the next, so filters compose into pipelines (`java RandomSeq 1000 | more`).
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan: the stream filter, a one-pass read-test-print loop that uses only a fixed number of variables. The value read is a most-recent holder and lo and hi are fixed values.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> RedirectionIsArgument: A filter keeps the relative order of the values it passes (it outputs a subsequence). Filters can be chained in any number without changing each other.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): A filter is the right tool when each output depends only on the current value, or on a fixed amount of state. Tasks that need all the values (sorting, k-th smallest, percentage above the mean) must store them in an array first.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Every value must pass the range test before it is output or processed. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Values outside lo..hi (e.g. negatives) are output because the test is missing or uses the wrong bounds or operators.
